blurb:
Kai is three months old, which basically means he's at peak kitten right now. Domestic medium hair, male, the kind of small that makes people stop and stare for a second before reaching out to pet him. If you've been on the fence about adding a cat to the house, there is no better time to adopt one than when they're this young. You get to shape the whole thing.

His listing is light on details since he's so new to the shelter, but kittens this age are generally adaptable. They figure out routines fast and tend to bond hard with whoever takes them home first. If you have kids or other pets, a young kitten introduced early usually does just fine with both.

Kai is at Lewisville Animal Services on College Pkwy. Walk-in visits are welcome. Go meet him before someone else does.

scoring_notes:
• Peak kitten appeal with broad family compatibility makes this the easiest adoption sell in the group
• Blurb is intentionally thin on backstory — novelty of youth replaces narrative depth
• Framed as brand new to the shelter with an urgency-to-act tone, suggesting minimal wait time

blurb:
Buck is four years old, 10 pounds, and already done with the kitten chaos phase of life. If you've ever thought about getting a cat but weren't sure you wanted to deal with a tiny creature bouncing off your walls at 2am, Buck is your answer. He's a full-grown domestic shorthair who knows what a litter box is for and has been using it reliably. That part's done.

He came in without much backstory, so his compatibility with other pets and kids is still an open question. That said, Lewisville Animal Services allows walk-in visits, so if you have animals at home and want to do a meet before you decide anything, that's an option.

He's vaccinated, microchipped, neutered, and flea-treated — all the upfront stuff is handled. If you're looking for a mellow, low-drama addition to your home, Buck is the move. Head to College Pkwy in Lewisville and go say hi.

• Low-maintenance adult cat fully vetted and past the chaotic kitten phase — strong pitch for busy households

blurb:
That name alone should tell you something. Simon Kitty Paws is a two-year-old domestic shorthair with a name that sounds like he introduced himself and nobody argued with it. He's 13 pounds, which means he's got some size to him — not chunky, just substantial. The kind of cat that takes up the whole armrest when he decides it's his.

He's litter box trained and fully vetted — vaccinated, microchipped, neutered, and flea-treated. Everything's already handled. His compatibility with other pets and kids is unknown since he came in without much history, but the shelter does walk-in visits so you can bring your crew and see how introductions go before you commit.

If you're looking for a cat with a little personality baked into his name and probably the rest of him too, Simon Kitty Paws is worth a stop. Lewisville Animal Services is on College Pkwy in Lewisville. Walk in during visiting hours and ask for him by his full name. He deserves that.
